what: Karpathy's experiment: hand an AI agent a small but real LLM-training setup (a simplified single-GPU nanochat) and let it edit the training code autonomously overnight, keeping only the changes that lower validation bits-per-byte.
architecture: The harness is program.md, 'a super lightweight skill': the agent cuts a branch autoresearch/<tag>, then LOOP FOREVER — edit train.py, git commit, run `uv run train.py > run.log 2>&1`, extract results with `grep "^val_bpb:\|^peak_vram_mb:" run.log`, log an untracked results.tsv row (commit, val_bpb, memory_gb, keep/discard/crash, description), keep the commit if val_bpb dropped, otherwise git reset. Runs over 10 minutes are killed and reverted; crashes are logged as status 'crash' with val_bpb 0.000000. A NEVER STOP clause forbids pausing to ask the human — ~12 experiments/hour, ~100 per night.

Scope split over exactly three files: the agent may edit only train.py — 'everything is fair game' (architecture, optimizer, hyperparameters, batch size, model size; baseline is DEPTH 8 → 512-dim, Muon at lr 0.04 for matrices + Adam for embeddings 0.6 / unembedding 0.004 / scalars 0.5, total batch 2^19, 'SSSL' sliding-window attention, FA3 kernels). prepare.py is read-only, no new packages allowed.

The gate is evaluate_bpb in prepare.py ('DO NOT CHANGE — this is the fixed metric'): validation bits-per-byte on a pinned shard (shard_06542 of climbmix-400b-shuffle), ~21M eval tokens (EVAL_TOKENS = 40 × 524,288) at MAX_SEQ_LEN 2048 — sums per-token cross-entropy in nats over target byte lengths, special tokens excluded; vocab-size-independent so architecture changes compare fairly.

Fixed 300-second wall-clock training budget (first 10 compile/warmup steps excluded) keeps every experiment directly comparable and auto-tunes to your GPU; training fast-fails if loss is NaN or > 100. Soft constraints: VRAM shouldn't blow up, and a simplicity criterion — a ~0.001 val_bpb gain for 20 hacky lines is 'probably not worth it', while equal-or-better results from deleting code is a win.
Baseline printed by the stock config (example in program.md): val_bpb 0.997900, 953 steps, 499.6M tokens, 50.3M params, 44.0 GB peak VRAM, 39.8% MFU in 300.1s on an H100.
advantages: Time-boxed equal-budget comparisons: because every run costs exactly 5 minutes regardless of what changed, results stay comparable across radical architecture rewrites, and the search finds the best model for your specific hardware rather than a leaderboard config.

Cleanly separates what evolves from what judges: train.py (agent-editable), prepare.py (immutable evaluator), program.md (human-editable 'research org code') — so you can study or iterate on the improvement policy itself, not just the code it improves.
Fully auditable by construction: each experiment is a git commit on the run branch plus a results.tsv row, keeping diffs reviewable and the overnight history replayable.
run: Install uv (`curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh`), then: `uv sync`; `uv run prepare.py` (one-time data + BPE tokenizer, ~2 min); `uv run train.py` (one ~5-min experiment). For autonomous mode, spin up Claude/Codex in the repo with all permissions disabled and prompt: 'Hi have a look at program.md and let's kick off a new experiment! let's do the setup first.'
note: Read program.md first — the loop, keep/discard rule, crash policy, and NEVER STOP clause are the entire harness; then evaluate_bpb in prepare.py, the gate the agent may not touch. Distinct from the AutoResearch paper (arXiv 2608.17906).
